name: Admiral John Poindexter

summary.text: John M. Poindexter, a retired rear admiral, was President Reagan's national security adviser during the Iran-Contra affair. He was convicted in 1990 on charges arising from the affair; the D.C. Circuit overturned the convictions in November 1991 on the ground that his trial had been tainted by his immunised congressional testimony, and the Supreme Court declined review in December 1992. From 2002 to August 2003 he directed DARPA's Information Awareness Office, home of the Total Information Awareness programme; he resigned effective 29 August 2003 amid controversy over the office's projects, including a proposed terrorism futures market.

facts.claim: The Independent Counsel's final report records that Poindexter's Iran-Contra convictions were overturned on appeal in November 1991 and that the U.S. Supreme Court declined to review the case in December 1992.
facts.quote: In November 1991, Poindexter's convictions were overturned on appeal. In December 1992, the U.S. Supreme Court declined to review the case.

facts.claim: The D.C. Circuit's two-to-one decision overturned the convictions on the ground that the trial had been tainted by Poindexter's immunised congressional testimony.
facts.quote: the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia overturned Poindexter's convictions on the ground that his trial had been tainted by his immunized Congressional testimony

sources.publisher: Independent Counsel for Iran/Contra Matters (Lawrence E. Walsh), Final Report, Chapter 3 (FAS mirror)

facts.claim: Poindexter headed DARPA's Information Awareness Office, which studied computer-based information gathering for the post-9/11 counterterrorism effort; the office was disbanded in 2003 following widespread concern that its work would lead to intrusive government surveillance of U.S. citizens.
facts.quote: The IAO was disbanded in 2003, following widespread concern that its work would lead to intrusive Government surveillance of U.S. citizens.

facts.claim: Poindexter's resignation letter, dated 12 August 2003 and addressed to DARPA director Anthony Tether, announced his departure as director of the Information Awareness Office effective 29 August 2003; in it he defended the office's projects.
facts.quote: He says he will resign as director of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency's Information Awareness Office effective August 29

sources.title: Resignation Letter of John M. Poindexter
In his resignation, Poindexter defends projects

facts.claim: The Washington Times reported on 31 July 2003 that a defense official said the furor over Poindexter's involvement in the Iran-Contra scandal had made it too difficult to get a dispassionate hearing for his concepts, after public outcry over the proposed Policy Analysis Market terrorism futures project.
facts.quote: furor over his involvement in the 1980s Iran-Contra scandal had made it too difficult to get a dispassionate hearing for his unorthodox concepts

sources.title: Poindexter to resign over terrorism futures market

facts.claim: On 31 July 2003 Senators Wyden and Dorgan continued their call for closure of the Terrorism Information Awareness programme.
facts.quote: Wyden, Dorgan continue call for closure of Terrorism Information Awareness program
